title: Chasing the Moon's Shadow
explanation:
# Total Solar Eclipse from 50,000 Feet

NASA's specially equipped WB-57F aircraft chased the Moon's shadow across Iceland at 50,000 feet, positioning itself perfectly to capture the Sun's ghostly corona (its outer atmosphere) blazing above the clouds during a total solar eclipse on August 12. From this vantage point high in the stratosphere, cameras recorded stunning eclipse data while Venus, Jupiter, and Mercury became visible in the darkened daytime sky—a view impossible to achieve from the ground, where clouds and atmospheric haze normally block the view.
